 Unofficial results: Ada-Calvo wins Adelup, Limtiaco takes Congress, Tydingco new AG 
 Unofficial results from the Guam Election Commission have the Republican Ada-Calvo team winning the race for Adelup with a 3.3-point lead over Democrat team Terlaje-Perez, with all voter precincts counted up as of about 1:30 a.m. on Wednesday. 
 Sen. Therese Terlaje told supporters she called Vice Speaker Tony Ada to concede on behalf of the team. 
 At the Ada-Calvo camp, supporters cheered as lieutenant governor candidate EJ Calvo opened a bottle of champagne in celebration.
 Earlier in the night, Terlaje-Perez was up by just 80 votes. 
 As of 1:30 a.m., the Republican team had 15,945 votes while the Democrat team won 14,925 votes, with 59 of 59 precincts counted. Ada-Calvo held 51.45% of the vote to 48.15% for Terlaje-Perez. 
 Democrat candidate Alicia Limtiaco held on to her early lead over Republican incumbent Del. James Moylan at the end of the night. Limtiaco had 15,645 votes, 51% of votes cast, to the 14,983 cast for Moylan, who held 48.84% of the vote. 
 In the race for the attorney general, attorney Phillip Tydingco kept his lead to unseat second-place holder incumbent Attorney General Douglas Moylan.
 Here were the results for the AG race: 
 Tydingco: 11,583, 38.29%
 Moylan: 10,008, 33.08%
 Thomas Fisher: 3,842, 12.7%
 Peter Santos: 3,353, 11.08%
 Jordan Pauluhn: 1,448, 4.79%
 The race for the Legislature flipped, with Republicans taking eight of the top 15 spots to the seven held by Democrat candidates. Numbers were reversed earlier.

 1 a.m.: Ada-Calvo takes lead with 38 of 59 precincts counted, race still tight
 The Republican Ada-Calvo team took a 2.5-point lead over Democrat team Terlaje-Perez, with over two-thirds of all voter precincts counted up as of about 1 a.m. on Wednesday.
 Earlier in the night, Terlaje-Perez was up by just 80 votes.

 9:45 p.m.: Ballot count underway, first precinct tallied
 Guam Election Commission staff started feeding ballots into their vote counting machines, and one precinct from Yona was the first to see its ballots tabulated. 
 Ballots hit the machines around 9:30 p.m., about an hour earlier than they did during the Primary Election. 
 GEC Executive Director Maria Pangelinan said they were looking to keep the count going smoothly, but declined to predict when the final results might come out. 
 9:30 p.m.: Terlaje-Perez team arrives at camp
 The Democratic team of Sens. Therese Terlaje and Sabina Perez arrived at their Hagåtña campaign headquarters before 9:30 p.m. The team greeted their supporters and thanked them. They opened the food table with a prayer.
 8:30 p.m. Ballots arrive at UOG for counting 
 Just over 30 minutes after polls closed around the island, officials from Precinct 11A, Chalan Pago-Ordot, arrived at the University of Guam Calvo Field House with ballot boxes in tow.
 A steady stream of school buses hauling ballots and officials from other precincts were right behind 11A.
 Officials from 11A reported a good turnout compared to this year's Primary Election, and smooth going the whole day.
 The Guam Election Commission will have to give precinct officials the all-clear before they start running ballots through their vote counting machines.
